notes:
1. Title "Money and rules both tighten around AI" and dek "...while governments adjust the rules for AI companies" say more than the sections. Source (PYMNTS, EU): the AI Act's "guardrails ... are capable of meeting the risk posed by rogue artificial intelligence agents", so the EU is keeping its rules, not adjusting them; The Decoder: the White House "has reversed its decision to block" AISI access, which loosens a block. Fix: a title and dek that fit, e.g. title "AI financing draws scrutiny as regulators hold or reverse course" and a dek saying a bank CEO describes closer scrutiny of AI financing while the EU says its rules are enough and the White House requires incident reports.
2. Section 2 says "we can ask that question of our own books this week". This invents a lender's own books and experience, and "who sits behind an AI deal and how it is structured" goes beyond the source. Source: "She warned that financially weaker companies could face credit rating downgrades as markets reassess their exposure to AI-related investments." Fix: drop "we can ask that question of our own books this week" and tie the lender point to the downgrade warning only, e.g. "For a lender, that is a reason to check which borrowers are most exposed to AI-related investments."
3. Section 4 says "At the same time, The Decoder reports...". The incident-reporting mandate is dated Friday 9 October (PYMNTS: "came Friday (Oct. 9)"); the AISI reversal is dated 12 October (The Decoder, Oct 12, 2026, citing the Daily Telegraph). Neither source puts the two at the same time. Fix: "Separately, The Decoder reports ..."
4. Section 4 heading "Washington asks for incident reports": the source says the White House is "requiring" companies to report and correct incidents and that the process "is not optional". "Asks" understates it. Fix: heading "Washington requires incident reports" (body keeps "reportedly").
5. Section 5 "Which of our own AI exposures would we want to explain first?" implies the writer is a bank with its own exposures (invented experience). Fix: address the reader, e.g. "Which of your own AI exposures would you want to explain first?"
